problem: Open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs (ConceptGraphs, HOV-SG, FSR-VLN, DualMap) expose each object through a single fused feature or committed label, so minority but task-relevant semantic hypotheses from multi-view observations are lost at task time and cannot be recovered without re-running perception.
motivation: Different views describe the same object inconsistently (occlusion, segmentation noise, VLM uncertainty), so the dominant label may be wrong while the correct concept remains in the observation history. Different tasks (closed-vocabulary segmentation vs free-form retrieval) also favor different readouts, and a top-ranked target is only a hypothesis that should be verified during execution.
key_idea: Defer semantic commitment: store per-observation phrases, reliability cues and frame-mask provenance in each object node alongside separate aggregate geometry/visual features, consolidate them into a vocabulary-independent belief, and let task-specific readouts and arrival-time verification make the decision.
insight: Retaining secondary hypotheses helps fixed-vocabulary projection: ScanNet200 mIoU rises from 0.1286 (visual-only) to 0.2107 (consensus), 0.2393 (early-commit) and 0.2742 (full belief). No single readout is best for navigation, where consensus and early-commit (60/78) beat belief-weighted (58/78), so readouts should be task-specific. Belief-construction ablations show that low-evidence regularization and reliability weighting matter most for navigation (removing regularization drops SR from 76.9 to 70.5), while synonym consolidation has only a small effect.
method: Object node state: each node stores point cloud, aggregate visual embedding, list of language observations (phrase, frame, mask, confidence, point count), concept-evidence vector, normalized support distribution, consensus text feature and a trust status; visual and language channels are never fused during mapping.

Evidence acquisition: Qwen3-VL-4B proposes phrases per frame, SAM 3 grounds them as masks, MobileCLIP2-S4 gives global-local CLIP features (following FSR-VLN), and depth back-projection gives per-mask point clouds.

Geometric-visual association: observations are merged into instances as connected components when radius-based point-cloud overlap >= 0.75 and visual cosine >= 0.85; semantic agreement is not used, favoring precision.

Semantic belief: weight w=c*sqrt(n), consolidate synonymous phrases by text-embedding clustering, apply pseudo-count smoothing (alpha=0.5) to get relative support p_ik, mark nodes degraded if fewer than 3 observations, and keep a belief-weighted consensus text feature.

Task-time readouts: free-form retrieval scores fuse the visual similarity and a language head (consensus / early-commit / belief-weighted) with reliability-dependent lambda (1.0/0.7/0.2); fixed-vocabulary projection refines the belief with visual evidence within its retained support and projects concepts to benchmark classes via softmax affinities.

Execution-grounded correction: after navigating to the candidate, check visibility (with one bounded re-observation), query-mask similarity and geometric overlap; a failing candidate is excluded only for the current query and the unchanged query is re-grounded over the remaining candidates (K_max=2), without modifying the graph.
Navigation interface: object point cloud is projected onto the traversability map, and a nearest collision-free boundary pose is executed by a conventional Nav2 global/local stack.

setting.observation: posed RGB-D stream (plus LiDAR on the real robot)
setting.action_space: navigation goal poses executed by a conventional global/local planner (Nav2 on the real robot)
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (HM3D scenes with inserted YCB objects); ScanNet200 and Replica for segmentation; real Unitree G1
setting.privileged: none (posed RGB-D input for mapping; ground-truth poses assumed as in the DualMap protocol)

results: Full-belief projection improves mIoU over matched early-commit (0.2742 vs 0.2393 on ScanNet200, 0.2912 vs 0.2701 on Replica) and over DualMap (0.1604 and 0.2538). In HM3D-YCB navigation, consensus and early-commit reach 76.9% SR@1m, above DualMap at 70.5%. On the real Unitree G1, correction raises confirmation from 6/10 to 8/10.
limitations: Small-scale evaluation: 3 HM3D scenes with 78 trials, a 10-case real-world pilot, and static scenes only; the gaps between readouts on navigation are small, 2 to 4 trials.

Correction only handles cases where the intended target remains mapped: no absent-target rejection, no dynamic-map repair, and it assumes the navigation stack reaches the goal viewpoint; the confusable case only reaches 3/5.
The belief-weighted readout does not beat the simple consensus or early-commit readouts in navigation, and mapping is offline and depends on heavy foundation models.
